name: fix-this-test
description: Fixes one failing Python (pytest) test. Paste the pytest failure output and the test and source files (each starting with a line like `# file: src/money.py`). It reproduces the failure by running your pasted code with pytest in a locked-down sandbox inside its own container (no credentials, CPU, memory and time limits; outbound network is not blocked by the agent), lets the model read, edit and re-run in a short bounded loop, and returns a unified diff computed by code plus whether the fix was verified by a real re-run. It fixes the code, not the test: edits that weaken a test (removing asserts, skipping, changing expected values) are refused. It never says a fix works unless the re-run passed, and it writes nothing outside its own temporary run directory; you apply the patch yourself. Python and pytest only, standard library plus pytest. Not for writing features or new tests, code review, other languages or general programming questions.

skills.name: Fix a failing test
skills.description: From pasted pytest failure output and the test and source files: reproduce the failure in a sandbox, make the smallest source change that fixes the cause, re-run the tests and return a verified unified diff. Test-weakening edits are refused; nothing is written outside a temporary run directory.
examples: Fix this failing test: <pytest output> + `# file: tests/test_money.py` ... + `# file: src/money.py` ...
Why does this test fail? (no edits)
